summary: This lecture tells how Hamzah ibn Abdul Muttalib embraced Islam. The ustaz recalls the companions' return from Abyssinia and explains how Najashi understood Ja'far, with a discussion of lingua francas and companions like Zaid ibn Thabit who quickly learned Hebrew and Syriac. Next Abu Jahal threw filth at the Prophet SAW, and a slave woman told Hamzah, a strong hunter of about the same age as him. Hamzah grew angry and struck Abu Jahal with his bow and said he was on Muhammad's religion, though he had not planned to embrace Islam. That night he could not sleep, prayed for guidance, and next day pronounced the shahada before the Prophet SAW. The ustaz closes by promising the story of the second lion, Umar, and mentions Hamzah would fall as a martyr at Uhud.
keyPoints: Najashi understood Ja'far because Arabic was a trade language or through an interpreter.
Zaid ibn Thabit learned Hebrew in 15 days and Syriac in 17 at the Prophet's instruction.
Abu Jahal threw filth at the Prophet SAW and a slave woman told Hamzah, who was returning from hunting.
Hamzah struck Abu Jahal with his bow and said he was on Muhammad's religion.
After a sleepless night and a prayer for guidance, Hamzah pronounced the shahada before the Prophet SAW.

chapters.title: Hamzah strikes Abu Jahal
chapters.summary: The ustaz opens with Hamzah, a famous hunter, who struck Abu Jahal with his arrow.

chapters.title: Opening and recap
chapters.summary: The ustaz recalls Surah An-Najm, the companions' return from Abyssinia, and Quraysh pressing Abu Talib again.

chapters.title: Najashi's language and lingua franca
chapters.summary: Najashi may have understood Arabic through trade or used an interpreter, and the ustaz explains a lingua franca like Malay in the past.

chapters.title: Zaid ibn Thabit learns languages
chapters.summary: Zaid, who memorised 17 surahs from Mus'ab, was told to learn Hebrew and Syriac in days, and Salman came from Persia.

chapters.title: Guarding our own language
chapters.summary: We should learn other languages but guard our own, and the ustaz explains terms like Pak Long, Pak Ngah up to Pak Su.

chapters.title: Abu Jahal throws filth
chapters.summary: Quraysh pressed Abu Talib again and Abu Jahal threw filth at the Prophet SAW at Mount Safa with no one to help.

chapters.title: Hamzah, the strong hunter
chapters.summary: Hamzah, the Prophet's uncle and foster brother, loved riding, archery and hunting and kept a collection of trophies.

chapters.title: The lion of Allah
chapters.summary: Hamzah was about the Prophet's age, very strong and later called the Lion of Allah, but had not embraced Islam though he knew he was good.

chapters.title: The slave woman tells Hamzah
chapters.summary: A slave woman of Abdullah ibn Jud'an told Hamzah what Abu Jahal did to the Prophet SAW.

chapters.title: Hamzah is furious
chapters.summary: Hamzah put down his things and went looking for Abu Jahal who was laughing at the Kaaba.

chapters.title: Striking Abu Jahal
chapters.summary: Hamzah struck Abu Jahal's face with his arrow until it bled and his friends wanted to attack him.

chapters.title: I am on his religion
chapters.summary: Hamzah said he was on Muhammad's religion, so Abu Jahal calmed his friends, and Hamzah was startled since he had not planned it.

chapters.title: A sleepless night
chapters.summary: The Arabs were ashamed to retract their words, so Hamzah could not sleep thinking about what he said.

chapters.title: Hamzah's shahada
chapters.summary: Hamzah prayed for guidance and next day pronounced the shahada before the Prophet SAW, the 39th to embrace Islam in Mecca.

chapters.title: Recap and the second lion
chapters.summary: Hamzah means lion, and the ustaz promises the story of the second lion who embraced Islam as the 40th.

chapters.title: Q&A and Hamzah the martyr
chapters.summary: Umar had not yet embraced Islam and only Hamzah matched him. Hamzah would be martyred at Uhud and the Prophet SAW would weep.

dalil.translation: The Prophet SAW said that if one goes to Uhud and greets the martyrs, they will answer.
dalil.context: The ustaz cites this saying when mentioning Hamzah's grave at Uhud. He does not name a narrator or source.

people.role: Uncle and foster brother of the Prophet SAW
people.context: A strong hunter called the Lion of Allah, embraced Islam after striking Abu Jahal, and would be martyred at Uhud.
Threw filth at the Prophet SAW and was struck by Hamzah.
Wept hearing Ja'far, perhaps because he understood Arabic or through an interpreter.

people.role: Spokesman of the companions in Abyssinia
people.context: Spoke and recited Surah Maryam before Najashi.
Taught 17 surahs to Zaid ibn Thabit.
Memorised 17 surahs at age ten and learned Hebrew and Syriac in a matter of days.
Mentioned as an example of someone who learned Arabic.
Owner of the house where Hilf al-Fudul was made.
Mentioned in comparison with Hamzah, called the Lion of Allah.
Not yet Muslim when Hamzah embraced Islam and would embrace Islam as the 40th.

lessons.title: Bravely defending family
lessons.body: Hamzah was angry and defended his nephew who was insulted.

lessons.title: Keeping one's word
lessons.body: The Arabs were ashamed to retract their words, which set Hamzah thinking.

lessons.title: Praying for guidance
lessons.body: Hamzah prayed that Allah ease him into the religion if it was true.

lessons.title: The Quran calms the heart
lessons.body: Hamzah's heart grew calm when the Prophet SAW recited Quran and told about Allah.

lessons.title: Learning other languages
lessons.body: The companions learned other languages to understand and call to society.

lessons.title: Guarding one's own language
lessons.body: We should not abandon Malay and our family terms.

lessons.title: Keeping healthy and strong
lessons.body: Hamzah was strong and sharp, so we too need to eat well and sleep enough.

lessons.title: Help from family
lessons.body: The Prophet SAW had a strong and brave uncle to defend him.
